title: Correlated temperature spikes across multiple racks during generator test
description: Temperature sensors across 12 devices in 3 separate racks simultaneously reported readings 20-30°C above baseline during a 45-minute window. The spikes appeared suddenly, sustained for the full duration, then returned to normal. No physical environmental changes were detected in the facility. The event timing correlated with a scheduled monthly generator transfer test.
root_cause: During the generator transfer test, the facility's primary cooling system experienced a brief interruption (HVAC units reset during the power transition). While servers continued operating on generator power, the cooling system took 3-5 minutes to fully restart. The thermal mass of the equipment caused temperatures to rise rapidly without active cooling. The 45-minute duration represents the time for cooling to restore temperatures to baseline after the HVAC restart delay.
resolution_steps: Verify correlation between temperature events and facility power/generator test schedule
Confirm all temperature readings returned to baseline within expected timeframe post-event
Request facilities team add HVAC to critical power circuit that doesn't transfer during generator tests
If HVAC cannot be moved to critical power, implement pre-cooling protocol before scheduled generator tests
Add suppression rule for temperature alerts during scheduled generator test windows (±15 minutes)
Document expected thermal behavior during transfer events for operator awareness
